- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend + negative sentiment, model tends to overshoot downward; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent low.  
- After a spike in forecast (e.g., >+10% from prior 30d), reduce next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5% to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, add 1–3% upward bias to avoid missing short-term rebound.  
- Model often overestimates mean reversion in 30d horizon; if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with true mean.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), avoid extrapolating trend; use 3–5 day moving average of true values as anchor.
